event_lost_scroll_r1.why: 舊書攤老貓把卷軸橫舉在胸前、有手印圖解那面朝觀眾展示，他自己看的是背面；文字是老貓「一頁頁翻看筆記、推了推眼鏡」，圖解應該朝他自己。
event_lost_scroll_r1.scene: SETTING: the SAME old bookstall as in reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event), on a small patch of grey paving stones with a few tufts of grass: a small wooden stall with a slanted plank roof on two wooden posts, a hanging navy cloth banner with a pale cat-head emblem, and a wooden counter with a few stacked old books and rolled scrolls on it. Behind the counter stands the OLD BOOKSTALL KEEPER, exactly as in reference image 3: a plump brown tabby old cat with bushy white eyebrows, a white muzzle, small round wire glasses and a dark brown robe. He is EXAMINING the unsigned scroll: his LEFT paw holds the scroll up by its top wooden roller, so the unrolled paper hangs straight down in front of his chest, and the scroll is turned TOWARD HIMSELF - its side with the hand-seal diagrams and notes faces the keeper's own eyes, so the VIEWER SEES ONLY THE PLAIN, BLANK CREAM BACK of the paper (no drawings, no marks, nothing on the side we see). With his RIGHT paw he pushes his round glasses up his nose. His head is tilted down toward the paper and his eyes read it closely, eyebrows raised with interest. Qiuqiu stands on the paving stones beside the stall, facing the keeper, hugging in both paws a small brown cloth pouch stuffed with dried fish (a few dried fish tails poke out of its top) - the payment he has just received. Happy, pleasantly surprised face. QIUQIU'S FUR is the warm, slightly pinkish PALE CREAM of reference image 1 with soft grey-brown stripes - NOT cool grey, NOT grey-and-white.
